questions.question: When was the Preamble to the India Constitution last amended?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1976.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

__
 
• The Preamble to the India Constitution last amended in **1976.**

 
 
• It was amended by the **42ⁿd amendment act** of 1976.
 
• 42ⁿd amendment act was passed during the time of **Indira Gandhi government.**
 
• By the 42ⁿd amendment act three new words, **Socialist, secular, and integrity** were inserted to the preamble.
 
• The 42ⁿd amendment act of 1976 is known as **mini-constitution.**
 
 
 
• The preamble has been amended **only once** after its formation.
 
• The preamble of the Indian constitution is borrowed fro** American constitution.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

 
• Changes made by the 42ⁿd amendment act are:

 
 
• added a list of **10 fundamental duties **by adding a new part IV A.
 
• Made the president bound by the advice of the cabinet.
 
• Added part **XIV A** dealing with the administrative tribunals.
 
• Raised the tenure of Lok Sabha and state legislative assembly from** 5 years to 6 years.**
 
• Tried to give primacy to directive principles over fundamental rights.

questions.question: According to the Government of India’s submission and judicial interpretation, the Right to vote in India is:

options.text: A fundamental right guaranteed under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution.
A constitutional right derived directly from Part III of the Constitution.
A statutory right conferred by the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
A natural right inherent to every citizen above 18 years of age.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The Central Government clarified before the Supreme Court that the right to vote is only a statutory right, distinct from the freedom of voting, which stems from the right to expression under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The right to vote is conferred by Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 and is not a fundamental right. Hence, it exists only as long as the statute provides for it. **Hence, option C is correct. **
 
• The freedom of voting, however, — that is, the choice of whom to vote for or whether to vote at all — is considered an aspect of the freedom of expression protected under Article 19(1)(a).
 
• The Centre cited the Supreme Court judgment in People’s Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL) vs. Union of India (2003), which recognized the right to vote as statutory but the freedom of voting as a constitutional liberty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 2003 PUCL judgment also recognized the importance of the NOTA (None of the Above) option, as an expression of dissent.
 
• The right to vote can be restricted or regulated under statutory provisions, such as disqualification criteria in the RPA Act.
 
• The distinction reinforces that voting is an act governed by law, but choice in voting is a constitutional expression.

questions.question: The gravitational potential energy of an object at a point above the ground is defined as the work done in ________.

options.text: raising it from the ground to that point against gravity
allowing it to stand on the ground against gravity

questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**raising it from the ground to that point against gravity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The gravitational potential energy** of an object at a point above the ground is defined as the work done in raising it from the ground to that point against gravity.
 
• **Gravitational energy**, such as elevating objects against the gravity of the Earth, is the potential energy correlated with gravitational force.
 
• If an object falls within a gravitational field from one point to another point, the gravity force will do positive work on the object, and the gravitational potential energy will decrease by the same amount.
 
• Near the surface of the Earth, the product mgh is the work performed in raising an object through a height h, so** U = mgh**
 
• **The Newton's law of gravitation:** This law states that every point mass in the universe attracts every other point mass with a force that is directly proportional to the product of its masses and inversely proportional to the distance between them in the square.

questions.question: Under the updated Earthquake Design Code 2025, which newly introduced zone represents the highest seismic risk in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zone VI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **India released an updated Seismic Zonation Map under the Earthquake Design Code 2025, introducing a new highest-risk Zone VI covering the entire Himalayan arc.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zone VI is the newly created highest-risk seismic zone under the 2025 Earthquake Design Code.**
 
• **The zone covers the full Himalayan arc from Jammu & Kashmir–Ladakh to Arunachal Pradesh, the most tectonically active belt.**
 
• **The update replaces the 2016 map and recognises extreme seismic stress along the Indian–Eurasian Plate boundary.**
 
• **The new zonation ensures stricter building standards and safety compliance for high-risk regions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Probabilistic Seismic Hazard Assessment (PSHA)**__

 __
 
• Globally accepted scientific method used for the new seismic map.
 
• Incorporates probability, ground motion models, and tectonic data for accurate hazard estimation.
 
 
 
• **Change in Hazard Distribution**__
 __
 
• 61% of India’s landmass is now classified under moderate to high hazard zones.
 
• Earlier, 59% of the country fell in these categories.
 
 
 
• **Inter-Zone Boundary Rule**__
 __
 
• Towns located between two seismic zones will automatically shift to the higher-risk zone.
 
• Ensures stricter compliance and enhanced building safety.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Region Risk**__
 
 
• The Himalayas lie along the highly active Indian–Eurasian Plate collision zone.
 
• High tectonic stress makes it the most earthquake-prone region in India.

questions.question: Fundamental Rights are enumerated in which part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
Fundamental Rights is enumerated in part III of Indian Constitution.

 
• "Fundamental Rights" are the basic and inviolable rights of the common people.
 
• It ensures civil liberties so that all Indians can live in peace and harmony as citizens of India. 
 
• Some important fundamental rights are:

 
• Right to freedom (Article 19, 20, 21A and 22).
 
• Right to freedom of religion (Article 25 to 28).
 
• Right to constitutional remedies (This right is called as the “heart and soul of Indian constitution” by B.R Ambedkar (Article 32)).

questions.question: Which multicellular Eukaryotes have cell wall and they do not perform photosynthesis?
questions.solution:

• Fungi are heterotrophs as they acquire their food by absorbing dissolved molecules.
 
• Fungi are the only organisms that have **cell walls made of chitin.**
 
• The Plantae **are multicellular eukaryotes.**
 
• Animals are multicellular, eukaryotic organisms, which are heterotrophic.
 
• **Protista** is a group of all the eukaryotes that are not fungi, animals, or plants.
 
• Protists have a **nucleus containing their DNA.**
 
• The five-kingdom system was developed by Robert H. Whittaker in 1969.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The Union Government introduced the SHANTI Bill, 2025 in the Lok Sabha to overhaul India’s civil nuclear energy laws and allow private and joint venture participation in nuclear power generation for the first time since Independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The SHANTI Bill repeals the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010, creating a unified legal framework for civil nuclear energy.** Hence, Option 2 is correct. **
 
• It allows private and foreign participation while retaining state control over sensitive domains such as nuclear fuel, heavy water, and waste management. Hence, other options are incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Bill grants statutory status to the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB), enhancing regulatory independence and parliamentary accountability.
 
• It removes supplier liability and caps operator liability to align India with international nuclear liability conventions, boosting investor confidence.
 
• The Bill supports deployment of Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), aiding India’s clean energy transition and long-term energy security.
